errors: Axiom (b) is written 'X_i ≤ X_j'. It means inclusion X_i ⊂ X_j.

Stability of axioms (1) under arbitrary base change is correct: pullback preserves closed subobjects, unions and intersections, and preimages of locally finite families are locally finite. But the isomorphisms (3) for an ARBITRARY X' → X are too strong if the X_{Δ_r} are built from tubular neighbourhoods. The next page restricts accordingly: tubular neighbourhoods are defined only for X' open, and the compatibility is claimed for (proper) local immersions. Formulas (4) for R_ij and S_ij are stated there without that hypothesis. So (3) as written is a gap that Grothendieck himself corrects on the following page.

ideas.what: Axioms for a poset-indexed closed stratification: locally finite closed X_i, monotone, covering, with X_i ∩ X_j equal to the union of the X_k for k ≤ i, j.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space / continuous map X → I (Alexandrov topology), à la Lurie HA Appendix A
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratifications informally; these exact axioms are not known to be published.

ideas.what: Base change of a stratification along any X' → X.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of stratified spaces / stratified maps

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial system X_{Δ_r}, indexed by chains of I, of elementary topoi (tubes X_Δ, restrictions to strata X^*_Δ, deleted tubes / links dot-X_Δ), and its compatibility with base change.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of strata and (iterated) homotopy links indexed by the subdivision sd(I); décollages
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn, Hughes (homotopy links); Haine; Barwick–Glasman–Haine (exodromy, décollages, ~2018–2020)

missed.claim: Grothendieck organises the reconstruction data of a stratified topos as a semi-simplicial system indexed by chains Δ_r of the stratifying poset (tubes, strata, links), and wants it compatible with base change. This anticipates the décollage / sd(P)-indexed link diagrams of Haine and Barwick–Glasman–Haine, together with their pullback functoriality.
missed.quote: D'ailleurs le système ½ simpl. des X_{Δr} a comme image inverse celui des X'_{Δr}, défini par les X'_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows a topos-level (rather than ∞-categorical) version of the link-diagram description of stratified spaces, conceived around 1981. This is historically relevant for crediting the exodromy and décollage picture. Mathematically, though, it is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine base-change stability check. Its interest lies in the framework it serves, a chain-indexed system of tubes and links reconstructing X, which prefigures modern exodromy and décollage work. But the content here is elementary, and the strong claim (3) is qualified on the next page.
